Last summer, the fair maps movement won big at the Supreme Court in Allen v. Milligan. The ruling protected Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and led to new maps across the region. subject: What we need after Trump’s rally in Phoenix
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Trump and Lake’s supporters are lighting us up online — the attacks are pouring in. If that’s any indication, it means Trump and Lake are raising a ton of money, too.
#

Peter, we launched a 48 hour fundraising drive during the DNC on Thursday.
Now, we’re extending that fundraising drive after Donald Trump’s rally with Kari Lake in Phoenix last night, because he came at Ruben with his most vicious broadside of the entire campaign.
He called Ruben a “maniac” multiple times. He said Ruben “shouldn’t even be allowed to run” against Kari Lake. He said if he wins in Arizona, he wins the presidency.
We’re already seeing the impact. Trump and Lake’s supporters are lighting us up online — the attacks are pouring in. If that’s any indication, it means Trump and Lake are raising a ton of money, too.
Ruben’s already got $12 million in television ads coming his way. Millions more could do serious damage. The way we fight back starts with emails like these.
If everyone reading this right now chipped in, we’d absolutely destroy our fundraising goals for the month. We wouldn’t need to ask again for weeks. But that’s the issue — not everyone can chip in.
So we’re asking you, Peter, someone who has been with us for awhile to make that donation. We know you understand how important this race is, and we’re counting on you to dig deep and help Ruben fight back.
How about it?
[**Can you chip in $5 (or perhaps more) to Ruben Gallego’s campaign?**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-august24.kZit_I&refcode=em240824-1-160&t=1&akid=2932%2E734936%2EI5VIp1)

And I want to make one thing clear: **If we lose this race, there will be no way that Democrats will control the Senate — not a chance.**

So I need your help. We need to deploy volunteers to every corner of Maryland to win over undecided voters and defeat Larry Hogan and his MAGA allies to hold Maryland’s Senate seat blue.

subject: There’s an important race happening in my home state this year

body:
[1]Lucas Kunce for U.S. Senate

[ https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/68688?refcode=em20240824-7433&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1001&akid=7433%2E614464%2EeoMQX4 ]Photo of Jon Hamm.

Hey Peter,
it’s Jon Hamm.

There’s an important U.S. Senate race happening in my home state this year
that I think you need to know about.

So before I ask you to chip in toward my friend Lucas Kunce’s campaign to
defeat Josh Hawley and flip Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat, please let me
explain why no one can afford to sit on the sidelines in this race.

[ https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/68688?refcode=em20240824-7433&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=7433%2E614464%2EeoMQX4 ]DEFEAT JOSH HAWLEY

Let’s start at the beginning. When I first got to know Lucas, his story
resonated with me. He’s a born-and-raised Missourian who knows the real
value of community — helping each other out, for better or for worse.

Growing up, his parents went bankrupt from his youngest sister’s medical
bills and his family survived on the support of their friends and
neighbors. After getting to college on a Pell Grant, Lucas decided to join
the U.S. Marine Corps to honor the community that had given his family so
much. He served for 13 years, including three deployments to Iraq and
Afghanistan before later being stationed at the Pentagon.

Once he left active duty, Lucas turned his focus to the corrupt
politicians and corporate monopolies that dominate our economy and squeeze
small businesses. He took on everyone from Big Tech and Big Ag to defense
contractors and pharmaceutical companies.

Now, Lucas is running to defeat January 6th coward Josh Hawley and take
back Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat for real, everyday people.

[ https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/68688?refcode=em20240824-7433&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=7433%2E614464%2EeoMQX4 ]ELECT LUCAS KUNCE

Let’s just be clear here: Hawley’s January 6th cowardice isn’t the only
reason he’s incapable of representing my home state.

Since he was elected to office, Josh Hawley hasn’t fought to bring even
$0.01 back to our communities — but he’s had plenty of time to make money
for himself.

[ https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/68688?refcode=em20240824-7433&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1004&akid=7433%2E614464%2EeoMQX4 ]Business Insider excerpt about Hawley's profits from book sales: The
Missouri senator's annual financial disclosure, filed last week, indicated
that he made $127,500 from book royalties in 2023. It is unclear whether
that sum includes an advance for Hawley's forthcoming book or also
includes composed of royalties from the senator's previous books. In 2021,
Hawley made $467,000 in book royalties. Headlines from KC Star and
Missourinet about Hawley's refusal to invest in Missouri.

While giant corporations strip our state of opportunity and jack up
prices, Hawley is only focused on enriching himself. He’s made hundreds of
thousands of dollars more than his congressional salary by selling his
weird book all about "Manhood."

All this, while he made taxpayers cover the cost of his own lawbreaking.

[ https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/68688?refcode=em20240824-7433&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1005&akid=7433%2E614464%2EeoMQX4 ]St. Louis Post-Dispatch headline: MO taxpayers paid more than $250,000
for Josh Hawley's open records violations.

Missouri can’t afford another six years of Hawley in the
Senate, Peter, and voters of
all stripes seem to agree.

Morning Consult reported that Josh Hawley has the lowest approval rating
of any Republican incumbent up for re-election this November. And even
Hawley’s own former mentor, Missouri’s three-term Republican U.S. Senator
Jack Danforth, said supporting Hawley was “the worst decision I’ve ever
made in my life.”

After spending a whole year consolidating support from workers, community
leaders, and organizations across Missouri, Lucas Kunce has more than
proved that he has what it takes to win this race. Multiple polls even
confirm he’s in a dead heat with Hawley. That’s why I’m asking for your
help, Peter:

[ https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/68688?refcode=em20240824-7433&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1006&akid=7433%2E614464%2EeoMQX4 ]Will you join me in supporting my friend Lucas Kunce by chipping in $10

name: Dr. Robert Jeffress
subject: Are you ready for the end times?
body:
| | Please see a special message from our sponsor.
---
| | | | [](http://trk.libertyledger._c291cmNlX2NvZGU9V0VCJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9cHJvc3BlY3RpbmcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bXlzdGVyaWVzX2VuZF90aW1lcyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BRS1MTE81MzgxOCJ9/dhd7Mf2RRG3uVylDi5q8dw)
---
Hello Friend,

Take a moment to look around. It's like we're living out Romans 1:25 - trading the truth of God for a lie and focusing on earthly things rather than our Creator.

Have you ever wondered if things could return to God's original plan?

I want to remind you, Friend, that this chaotic time is fleeting. The shadows will fade, and a new day will dawn. The King of Kings, our Savior, will return.

That's the heart of Revelation.

Each day on this earth shapes us for what's to come - a grand finale. Amidst today's messiness and uncertainty, remember the promise that our story's end is already secured, regardless of the present turmoil or future darkness.

Revelation intricately unveils where our stories lead.

It's a captivating book filled with symbols, creatures, and events yet to unfold. But remember Revelation 1:3 - there's a blessing for those who read, listen, and follow its words because the time is near.

This isn't just a prophecy; it's a blessing-filled journey.

Revelation isn't just about revealing future events; it's about revealing Jesus Christ.

When Jesus came as a man, His divine brilliance was veiled by humanity. It's like dimming a lamp's light. But when He returns, that veil will lift, and we'll see His true glory. That's Revelation's essence.

As the great reveal approaches, I'm here to guide you and your loved ones through the remarkable events preceding the revelation of our King.

In my brand-new book, _Mysteries of the End Times: 5 Truths About God's Future Plans_ , I tackle five common questions about the end times. We'll delve into:

1\. America's Fate: Will America stand for Christ or fall for the Antichrist?
2\. The Day of the Lord: How should we live in anticipation of this apocalyptic event?
3\. The Marriage of the Lamb: What unfolds before and after the rapture?
4\. Gog and Magog: How can we honor God in our lives amid their appearance?
5\. The Tree of Life: What's the significance of this tree in the New Jerusalem?

Understanding these mysteries will anchor you in hope, bolster your trust in God's promises, and equip you to share with the unsure.

In addition to this new book, I would like to share with you "The Major Characters of the End Times," as a token of my gratitude for your support. This full-color, large print booklet introduces key players during the rapture, tribulation, second coming, and final judgment - vital for understanding the grand narrative.
[](http://trk.libertyledger._c291cmNlX2NvZGU9V0VCJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9cHJvc3BlY3RpbmcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bXlzdGVyaWVzX2VuZF90aW1lcyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BRS1MTE81MzgxOCJ9/fG-C3OZ5_ks4upYXrcnZ7w)I would like to send you my brand-new book _Mysteries of the End Times: 5 Truths About God's Future Plans_ and my brand-new resource "The Major Characters of the End Times" as a thank you for your generous support of $10 or more to the ministry of _Pathway to Victory_.

Make your generous gift here: [https://secure.ptv.org/mysteries-of-the-end-times-generous-gift-1-dr-robert-jeffress](http://trk.libertyledger._c291cmNlX2NvZGU9V0VCJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9cHJvc3BlY3RpbmcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bXlzdGVyaWVzX2VuZF90aW1lcyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BRS1MTE81MzgxOCJ9/Bwryg1aQxeSypuRBgy6e1g)

_Pathway to Victory_ is committed to equipping believers with biblical teaching and reaching the unsaved by spreading the Good News of Jesus Christ through the most effective means available: radio, television, digital, and print. Your gifts fuel that important work and enable people worldwide to experience an intimate walk with Christ. Thank you for your faithful support.

May our study of Revelation prepare, strengthen, and inspire you. Come quickly, Lord Jesus.

Sharing the Truth of God's Word, ____
---
| | Dr. Robert Jeffress Senior Pastor, First Baptist Dallas

I'm running for president because I believe in the promise of America.
I believe in a future where every person has the opportunity to not just get by, but to get ahead. Where health care is a fundamental right. Where women have the freedom to make decisions about their own bodies. Where people are free to love who they love openly and with pride. Where we have the freedom to be safe from gun violence. Where no one is above the law. And where our democracy and institutions are revered and protected.
That is the future that I am fighting for.
We love our country. We believe in the promise of America, and we are willing to fight for it.
**That fight requires more than just winning the White House in November.**
We need strong Democrats in state legislatures across the country so we can build on the progress we have made and work to deliver on the promise of our great nation.
This past week in Chicago, Democrats all across the country came together to celebrate our progress and plan for the hard work we need to do in the final 73 days before the election. We. Will. Win. subject: Liars and creeps don't belong in the U.S. Senate

body:
Floridians know all about creepy because of Rick Scott
| | |
---
Friend,

Let's be real here: Floridians know all too well what creepy is.

**It's Rick Scott. He's a creep. **

It's creepy how intent he is on controlling women's bodily autonomy and reproductive choices. He has pushed time and again for a national abortion ban, and would lead the charge in getting such legislation signed into law if Donald Trump gets reelected to the White House.
It's creepy how he voted against the Right to IVF Act, which would have guaranteed federal protections for the procedure. And it's creepy how he _lied about that vote_ — spending millions of dollars on an ad buy saying he would protect access to that very procedure a day after he voted to do the opposite!
The U.S. Senate is one of our world's greatest democratic bodies. It's not a place for creeps and liars, particularly those like Rick Scott intent on pushing the GOP's radical Project 2025 agenda.
**We can and must defeat him: Last time around, Rick Scott spent $64 million of his own money to buy Florida's Senate seat — and he _barely scraped by_ , winning by just over 10,000 votes.**

Look, I'm building coalitions that are much larger than 10,000 votes, and right now, I'm statistically tied with Rick Scott in the polls. But I can't cut my campaign a check for $64 million, nor would I if I could. This is a people-powered movement, and it's _your_ support I need to defeat Rick Scott.
**[So, friend, will you rush a donation of $5 or whatever you can spare to help defeat creepy Rick Scott in Florida and defend our Democratic Senate majority? My unit was the hardest-hit Marine battalion of the entire war. But the fight didn’t end there. Instead, my brothers and I found that we had a whole other fight ahead of us: the fight to get the care we were promised. The care we earned.
**But I never lost hope. I took on the work myself. I figured out how I could get my guys recognition, their services, their disability payments. I went to Congress to change the system, to make sure it lived up to the promises we make to the people who serve, and to their families. **
I slept by a burn pit while I was in Iraq, and countless others did the same. Guys I deployed with, healthy, strong guys, came down with serious illnesses because of those burn pits.
After a long, tough fight, we passed the PACT Act to provide benefits for veterans with those toxic exposures. And now, more than a million veterans from multiple generations are finally getting the help they need.
**Trump had four years to get that bill done, and he didn’t. He dodged the draft himself and made some other guy take his place. He called fallen Marines from World War I buried in France “suckers” and “losers.” Just last week, he insulted the few who earned our nation's most sacred military honor, the Medal of Honor.**
He and Kari Lake want you to believe our military and our veterans have no greater champion. But they don’t care about us. Theirs is the same record that landed my guys back home needing to scrape and claw for PTSD treatment, for health care, for basic dignity.

But I can’t do it alone. In everything I’ve accomplished in life, I’ve always had a team behind me. You are a critical part of that team, friends. And today, I need your help.

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Something is very wrong when a Republican millionaire and
billionaire-backed lobby group and its super PAC can buy elections and
oust sitting members of Congress for the sake of protecting their own
interests.

We saw it happen this summer when AIPAC spent $25 million to successfully
defeat Justice Democrats incumbents Rep. Jamaal Bowman and Cori Bush, two
of the only Black, working-class, progressive leaders we have in Congress.

And it’s not just our progressive movement that’s at risk: as Rep. Summer
Lee pointed out, AIPAC’s assault is not just on the Squad, but on the
Democratic Party and our democracy as a whole.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240824.V613ri&refcode=em20240824-35935&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=35935%2E1203867%2EsnE8Kr ]X post by Summer Lee reading, in part, “Let's start by just being
clear: when we're talking about this assault, it isn't on the Squad, it's
not on progressives—it's on democracy.”

Senator Bernie Sanders made this same point on the national stage at the
DNC this week, reminding us of the ongoing, urgent need to stop dark
money’s dangerous influence on our government and politics:

“At the very top of the to-do list is the need to get big money out of our
political process. Billionaires in both parties should not be able to buy
elections, including primary elections. For the sake of our democracy, we
must overturn the disastrous Citizens United Supreme Court decision and
move toward public funding of elections.”

From the very beginning, Justice Democrats has led the call to get
corporate dark money out of our elections and urge the Democratic Party to
reject AIPAC once and for all — and we’re keeping up that fight until we
win.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jdem-20240824.V613ri&refcode=em20240824-35935&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=35935%2E1203867%2EsnE8Kr ]We’re continuing to support and rebuild our bloc of diverse,
working-class, progressive leaders who are committed to putting people —
not super PACs and corporate profits — first. But we can’t do it without
grassroots support from people like you. Please, if you can, fuel our
efforts with a contribution of $5 or more today.

body:
This dude was elected at 25 years old. Recognize him?
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20240824&t=1&akid=1098%2E587540%2EfKh-RU)
Peter, this dude was elected at 25 years old. Recognize him? 🎩
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240824?refcode=em20240824&amount=5&refcode2=1098_587540_fKh-RU&akid=1098%2E587540%2EfKh-RU)
I know the media will never give Biden the credit he deserves but I just have to say the history student in me is still geeking out.
He faced unprecedented challenges – from the largest economic downturn since the depression to the largest pandemic since the Spanish flu. In three years, he not only got kids back in school, but got our economy on track growing faster than any of the G7 with the one of the lowest rates of inflation by far. (It was still high but far less than most countries.)
At the same time he passed the largest climate spending ever of any country in human history, brought chip manufacturing back to the US, added Finland and Sweden to NATO, created the first Office of Gun Violence Prevention ever that oversaw a 20% reduction in gun homicides in Q1 2024, passed the first federal gun law in 30 years that has stopped well over 800 high risk people from buying semi automatic rifles like the AR-15, put billions into school and community safety programs, and so much more.
I think the number one reason Biden was able to do this (besides incredible staff) was because he was first elected to the Senate when he was 29 and had over 50 years experience on the Hill by the time he became President.
Time and time again we see the sooner someone starts in elected office and the more experience they get the better the president they are:
* FDR was 28 when first elected in NY.
* LBJ was 28 when he was elected to Congress.
* Lincoln was 25 when he was first elected to the IL House.

That’s why I’m so excited to see what comes from the young candidates Leaders We Deserve endorses. All of them are generational leaders under 35 and all of them need your help to get their start in the critical races they are campaigning in RIGHT NOW.

body:
[ https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1001&akid=3448%2E35263%2EUrazCD ]TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE

Peter — I have a
personal story I’d like to share with you.

Growing up, I was diagnosed with a serious illness and spent three months
in the hospital.

When I got better, my grandparents, who raised me, wanted to make sure I
was protected in case I got sick again. But they couldn’t find any
insurance policies that would cover me in the future.

Not from any insurer. Not at any price.

That meant my grandparents had to pay for my health care out of pocket,
and they had to make significant sacrifices to do so — all because I had a
pre-existing condition.

I saw my grandparents stay up late at night, worried that I might fall ill
again and that they wouldn't be able to afford my care.

No one should ever have to go through that. But my story is not
unique, Peter, and
I knew they weren’t the only ones. That’s why I got into public service.

I’m one of 133 million Americans who have the label "pre-existing
condition" attached to our care — and before the Affordable Care Act was
passed, many of us could be denied coverage.

Now, insurance companies can no longer discriminate against someone based
on their pre-existing condition. I championed health reform and wrote the
amendment to allow young people to stay on their parent’s insurance plan
up to age 26. And when I meet with young people across Wisconsin, almost
every hand in the room goes up when I ask who is on their parent’s health
insurance.

So, you can imagine my frustration whenever Republicans attack our health
care and threaten protections for folks with pre-existing conditions —
including my opponent Eric Hovde, who called my amendment a “stupid idea”
and said young people on their parent’s health insurance need to “grow up
and move on.”

If Eric Hovde flips this seat and secures the Senate majority for
Republicans, the ACA will be on the chopping block and countless Americans
could find themselves in a place where insurance companies are putting
profits over people.

That’s not right. And that’s why I need your help to defeat him.

clean_body: [ ]TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE Peter — I have a personal story I’d like to share with you. Growing up, I was diagnosed with a serious illness and spent three months in the hospital. When I got better, my grandparents, who raised me, wanted to make sure I was protected in case I got sick again. But they couldn’t find any insurance policies that would cover me in the future. Not from any insurer. Not at any price. That meant my grandparents had to pay for my health care out of pocket, and they had to make significant sacrifices to do so — all because I had a pre-existing condition. I saw my grandparents stay up late at night, worried that I might fall ill again and that they wouldn't be able to afford my care. No one should ever have to go through that. But my story is not unique, Peter, and I knew they weren’t the only ones. That’s why I got into public service. I’m one of 133 million Americans who have the label "pre-existing condition" attached to our care — and before the Affordable Care Act was passed, many of us could be denied coverage. Now, insurance companies can no longer discriminate against someone based on their pre-existing condition. I championed health reform and wrote the amendment to allow young people to stay on their parent’s insurance plan up to age 26. And when I meet with young people across Wisconsin, almost every hand in the room goes up when I ask who is on their parent’s health insurance. So, you can imagine my frustration whenever Republicans attack our health care and threaten protections for folks with pre-existing conditions — including my opponent Eric Hovde, who called my amendment a “stupid idea” and said young people on their parent’s health insurance need to “grow up and move on.” If Eric Hovde flips this seat and secures the Senate majority for Republicans, the ACA will be on the chopping block and countless Americans could find themselves in a place where insurance companies are putting profits over people. Peter,

We can’t believe we even need to send this email.

It has come out that Joyce’s opponent in New Hampshire’s race for Governor was a Purdue Pharma lobbyist who called OxyContin a “miracle drug.”

New Hampshire has been hit extremely hard by the opioid epidemic, and we’ve been grappling with this crisis for decades. You don’t have to go far to find a story about a Granite Stater who has been impacted. That’s what makes this especially disheartening.

[Our opponent is funding her campaign with profits she made working for the opioid industry, and we need to ensure that Joyce has the funds to defeat a Purdue Pharma lobbyist. Granite Staters deserve a Governor who fights for them. But Joyce’s opponent didn’t just lobby on behalf of Purdue Pharma. Since at least 2011, she worked and lobbied for a Pain Clinic that was involved in a major prescription opioid kickback scheme that recovery advocates have called a “pill mill.”

clean_body: | | Friend, On Thursday night, history was made when Kamala Harris took the stage and accepted the Democratic nomination for President, reaffirming what I have always known about her: Kamala is, and always has been, for the people. From her days as a prosecutor to standing tall as Vice President, Kamala Harris has been laser-focused on taking care of our families, our communities, and our future. When I wrote my op-ed in Essence back in 2019, I knew Kamala was the perfect antidote to the false narratives that divided us. Her story, as a daughter of immigrants and as the second class to integrate Berkeley schools, is the American story. It is a story of resilience, grit, and dedication. Her speech last night was a rallying cry for all of us who believe in a better future — one where everyone, no matter who they are or where they come from, can thrive. body:
This is a picture of my mom and my three sisters watching me speak at the DNC on Thursday night. My immigrant mother raised the four of us on a secretary’s salary.
#

The American Dream is alive, Peter.
Just look:
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-august24.kZit_I&refcode=em240824-2-160&t=1&akid=2940%2E734936%2EKRo1a5)
This is a picture of my mom and my three sisters watching me speak at the DNC on Thursday night.
My immigrant mother raised the four of us on a secretary’s salary. I worked any job I could get to support the family. I slept on the floor, on the couch, on a roll-out mattress. I got into Harvard with no money, no connections. I fought in Iraq. And now, I’m running for the U.S. Senate in Arizona.
I believed it when I was a kid, and I believe it now:**Anything is possible in the United States of America.**
But there is no denying that the American Dream feels out of reach for far too many.
Kari Lake won’t fix that, and Trump won’t either. They’ll divide us further, cut taxes for their billionaire friends, and leave an economy that works for them — not working families, not the middle class.
It is up to us to keep the American Dream alive — to defend it, to strengthen it. And the best way we can do that right now is by defeating Trump and Kari Lake.
[**So, I’m asking you to make a donation to my campaign today. Whatever you can afford, even a donation as small as $1. Yes, even $1. “” _Montana is Democrats' toughest Senate seat to keep blue in 2024,” Sen. Gary Peters (D-Mich.) said Tuesday during an Axios House event on the sidelines of the Democratic National Convention_.”

If you ask any political reporter what Senate race they perceive to be pivotal in this November’s election, **they’ll tell you Montana.**

Ask any Democrat in the country what Senate race they perceive to be the most difficult to hold onto, and **they’ll tell you Montana.**

name: Lauren Cooley, Institute for Faith & Culture
subject: Vote Your Faith
body:
Please read the following message from our sponsor.

Friend,

In the 2024 Election, it's not a matter of right
versus left - it's a matter of right versus wrong.

Morality is on the ballot...

...and the Institute for Faith & Culture is working
hard to register thousands of new Christian voters before this
year's election.

Friend, will you stand with the Institute for
Faith & Culture ... and believers across America ... as you
pledge to VOTE YOUR FAITH in the 2024 Election?

Sign the pledge to VOTE YOUR FAITH

God's hand is evident in the founding and shaping
of America. Our Founding Fathers were profoundly influenced by
biblical principles and our Judeo-Christian heritage is woven in
every founding document.

Yet, the world wants Christians to believe that our
faith has no place in the public square.

You and I know the truth: the very heart of America
is rooted in the timeless truths of Scripture!

Above: The Institute for Faith & Culture prepares
young believers for leadership every year. Let's pray for the
next generation as they confront a hostile and secular world and
bring the light of Christ to their campuses!

Friend, today America's godly heritage is under
attack - and the Institute for Faith & Culture, the non-profit
ministry I'm proud to lead, is pushing back against the
anti-Christian forces at play in America every day.

In this important year, the Institute for Faith &
Culture is registering thousands of voters and ensuring they
understand their civic and Biblical responsibility to vote...

...because life, religious liberty, and
righteousness in our nation are too important to remain on the
sidelines.

Friend, I hope you'll join us in igniting a
NATIONWIDE revival in support of biblical values! Pledge today to
VOTE YOUR FAITH in the 2024 Election.

When you sign the "Vote Your Faith" pledge, you're
not just making a personal commitment - you're joining a movement
of believers who are determined to be the salt and light our
country so desperately needs.

That's why my request today is so urgent ... and so
important.

Sign the pledge to VOTE YOUR FAITH

Secularism and moral relativism are eroding our
shared values and our nation's culture. The next generation is
leaving the faith in droves, the Church's influence on culture
has waned, and a time of moral chaos and spiritual darkness has
all but taken over our country.

America is at a crossroads, and the decisions we
make in the coming years will have far-reaching consequences.

By signing this special pledge to VOTE YOUR FAITH,
you are joining a growing movement of believers who refuse to be
silent, who are determined to make a difference, and who are
committed to advancing Christian principles in every area of our
society.

Please stand with the Institute of Faith & Culture
and THOUSANDS of believers across the country, as you pledge to
VOTE YOUR FAITH in the 2024 election.

Thank you for your support. Please join me in
praying ceaselessly for America's future.

Lauren Cooley

Executive Director

Institute for Faith & Culture

Sign the pledge to VOTE YOUR FAITH

5555 North Federal Hwy

Fort Lauderdale, FL 33308

body:
Peter, weekend we sent out a survey asking what this team’s priorities are as we head into the 2024 election.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20240824-4233-footer&t=1&akid=4233%2E420207%2E12BsQZ)
Peter, last weekend we sent out a survey asking what this team’s priorities are as we head into the 2024 election. We were thrilled by how many of you shared your thoughts with us — so today we wanted to share the results!
[**Take a look below, and then pitch in $3 to help keep Pramila in Congress fighting for progressive priorities like these and more ⬇️**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20240824?refcode=em20240824&amount=3&refcode2=4233_420207_12BsQZ&akid=4233%2E420207%2E12BsQZ)
**More than three quarters of the respondents agreed that these six issues should be among our top priorities:**
* 82% — Taking bold action on climate change
* 81% — Taxing the rich
* 78% — Getting big money out of politics and ending Citizens United
* 77% — Protecting our democracy and elections
* 76% — Protecting abortion rights
* 75% — Gun safety

**Here’s the good news: Pramila agrees!** She’s proud to have sponsored and passed legislation that begins to address these issues and more, but she also knows we still have a long way to go and a lot more work to do.
**Now here’s the bad news: Big corporate interests don’t want us to make progress on _any_ of these issues.** And they’re spending big to help elect Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans in Congress who will stop us.
[**We need your help to fight back, Peter. Will you pitch in $3 or whatever you can today to help Pramila keep fighting for our progressive, people-first agenda in Congress?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20240824?refcode=em20240824&amount=3&refcode2=4233_420207_12BsQZ&akid=4233%2E420207%2E12BsQZ)

Thank you, Peter. And if you didn’t get a chance to respond to this survey, don’t worry! We send these out on a semi-regular basis, so you’ll have another opportunity soon.

In solidarity,
Jayapal HQ

My unit was the hardest-hit Marine battalion of the entire war. But the fight didn’t end there.
Instead, my brothers and I found that we had a whole other fight ahead of us: The fight to get the care we were promised. The care we earned.
But I never lost hope. I took on the work myself. I figured out how I could get my guys recognition, their services, their disability payments. I went to Congress to change the system, to make sure it lived up to the promises we make to the people who serve, and to their families.
I slept by a burn pit while I was in Iraq, and countless others did the same. Guys I deployed with, healthy, strong guys, came down with serious illnesses because of those burn pits.
After a long, tough fight, we passed the PACT Act to provide benefits for veterans with those toxic exposures. And now, more than a million veterans from multiple generations are finally getting the help they need.
Trump had four years to get that bill done, and he didn’t. He dodged the draft himself and made some other guy take his place. He called fallen Marines from World War I buried in France “suckers” and “losers.” Just last week, he insulted the few who earned our nation's most sacred military honor, the Medal of Honor.
He and Kari Lake want you to believe our military and our veterans have no greater champion. But they don’t care about us. Theirs is the same record that landed my guys back home needing to scrape and claw for PTSD treatment, for health care, for basic dignity.
They have no place leading this nation, and after all the progress we have made together over the last few years, it is on us to do everything we can to defeat them.
That’s what I told the audience at the Democratic National Convention, and that is why I am running for U.S. Senate in Arizona.
But I can’t do it alone. In everything I’ve accomplished in life, I’ve always had a team behind me. You are a critical part of that team, friends.
And today, I need your help.

clean_body: | | | Friends, I spoke to the Democratic National Convention about my service in the Marines, how that made me who I am today, and why I am running for U.S. Senate. = | | = My unit was the hardest-hit Marine battalion of the entire war. But the fight didn’t end there. Instead, my brothers and I found that we had a whole other fight ahead of us: The fight to get the care we were promised. The care we earned. But I never lost hope. I took on the work myself. I figured out how I could get my guys recognition, their services, their disability payments. I went to Congress to change the system, to make sure it lived up to the promises we make to the people who serve, and to their families. I slept by a burn pit while I was in Iraq, and countless others did the same. Guys I deployed with, healthy, strong guys, came down with serious illnesses because of those burn pits. After a long, tough fight, we passed the PACT Act to provide benefits for veterans with those toxic exposures. And now, more than a million veterans from multiple generations are finally getting the help they need. Trump had four years to get that bill done, and he didn’t. He dodged the draft himself and made some other guy take his place. He called fallen Marines from World War I buried in France “suckers” and “losers.” Just last week, he insulted the few who earned our nation's most sacred military honor, the Medal of Honor. He and Kari Lake want you to believe our military and our veterans have no greater champion. But they don’t care about us. Theirs is the same record that landed my guys back home needing to scrape and claw for PTSD treatment, for health care, for basic dignity. They have no place leading this nation, and after all the progress we have made together over the last few years, it is on us to do everything we can to defeat them. That’s what I told the audience at the Democratic National Convention, and that is why I am running for U.S. Senate in Arizona. But I can’t do it alone. In everything I’ve accomplished in life, I’ve always had a team behind me. You are a critical part of that team, friends. [](https://www.kennedy24.com?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=sense_of_victory_8_24_24_all_1&n=4)

Dear Peter,
Well it is official. Some of what you heard is true. I am suspending my presidential campaign activities, and removing my name from the ballot in a handful of swing states, in order to ensure my candidacy does not inadvertently prolong the damage being done by the anti-democratic corporate kleptocracy that is today’s Democratic Party.
As one of my supporters, I would like to tell you what went into my decision, so that you know that your support has not been in vain.
Indeed, it is with a sense of victory, not defeat, that I am suspending my campaign. Not only did we accomplish the supposedly impossible task of collecting a million signatures to get on the ballot, but we elevated key issues into the center of national politics. The most important of these are:
* Corruption of government agencies
* Children’s health and chronic disease.
* Ending the war machine, and
* Ending government censorship, surveillance, and information control.

When I entered the race 16 months ago, no candidate was speaking about these issues. Kamala Harris still doesn’t mention them, but Donald Trump does. To be sure, I disagree with President Trump on many issues. But on these key matters, he and the people around him are in agreement. I believe I can best serve these goals as part of a unity cabinet inside the Trump administration.
I am not naive. I know there is no guarantee that fine sentiments will translate into meaningful action. I have come to this decision through many days of meditation and prayer, during which I have cycled through all of the emotions and arguments that my supporters have expressed to me, from every direction.
I also want you to know that I am only suspending my campaign, not terminating it. My name will still be on the ballot in most states. If you live in a blue state, you can vote for me without harming or helping President Trump or Vice President Harris. In red states — the same applies. I encourage you to do so. And if enough of you vote for me and neither of the major party candidates win 270 electoral votes, I could still end up in the White House in a contingent election.
I know this decision will be hard for many of you to understand, who have not gone through the intense process I have. To learn more about my thinking and my intentions, please [watch this video](https://www.kennedy24.com?e=d33e868971601c1c714cfe0555abd394&utm_source=joinkennedy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=sense_of_victory_8_24_24_all_1&n=5) of yesterday’s press conference, in which I announced my decision to the nation.
Thank you for your support through this intense journey of a presidential campaign. I will continue to do everything in my power to redeem your trust.
| |
---
---
Sincerely,
Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.

Tina for Oregon [https://nvlupin.blob.core.windows.net/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92654/images/TinaForOregon-Logo-FullColor-white.png]
Hi Peter,
Welcome to my team’s monthly newsletter of what I’ve been up to this month, so you can be in the loop about the great work happening.
I know life can be busy, and your inbox can get filled up with political emails, so I appreciate any time you can dedicate to reading this newsletter each month.
Thanks!
— TK

Tina focuses on getting Oregon’s wildfires under control.

Tina meets with local fire officials [https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcixOZ0H9blDjnzI77vJnmq9a2C_YM-bUhPmroqeW8DlOw5FqSj6snAZ_YbJPt1HLSDQCBt2RODwVHZIqlj-u5qOk-lDm0KYrpjw8Szz9lihGfM3b4st6MXGF_AqylWCYcv39-yiOkx3MeOODd3s5xH3i5-?key=3tTunpdgT2tQYTmIdWuK7Q]

Wildfires have been a dangerous threat all summer. Governor Kotek declared a statewide wildfire state of emergency through September to allow the state to deploy additional resources to communities in need.

Governor and First Lady visit with the Burns Paiute Tribe.

Governor Kotek with Tribal youth [https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcKz0uWzdSzxTEEYuVaCeBrlAI5jjsUvPRfxRxC6L1bU6VmB2dQSFlvGe9S7hLehilIi9Ep6pnWftxGliKEhrCt5slkxYXftPco7Fm50ILvb5VCc5wVxzA-UzP7I2Pg_OeMDmITGmFKyrbgeZfAw7g8eGzV?key=3tTunpdgT2tQYTmIdWuK7Q]

Tribal youth taught Tina and Aimee how to craft traditional tule ducks. The day was part of Governor Kotek’s commitment to visit all of Oregon’s nine federally recognized sovereign Tribal nations in 2024.

Portland International Airport opens a new terminal.

Governor Kotek with Tribal youth [https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdbMhjZfmD-_zKl_nMyzMeOLSblijdAt6FgCKM-RIHHsrqBvhOMzv0UPqPSZtNSi7HNvUlmJ01CUSXGFb1MMGDyNlkSzOrJFPSZiC_pVw-3rEwoHKah2L06wC2ZB8lAIKIq1LSCD457Wz063oLZHABxXjBh?key=3tTunpdgT2tQYTmIdWuK7Q]

This is a transformative addition to an already-great airport. The new terminal at PDX was built with timber locally sourced and harvested with a commitment to sustainable methods, by thousands of Oregonians, to create a beautiful place that is truly Oregon.

Tina interviews with OPB’s Think Out Loud.

Governor Kotek being interviewed [https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc5czcka9Pky84j6TkE7l118zuAx6Mln0WZQqgHr5l7JK78RkVQwUGSqQ4pwC_nVZTD2csDbVZvJsGQSzWBQyXbuD3AxnFcS7aKMEFPLubtWKBx6n5ZL9MKke0Mm4iE9nMSWBahINCcpl9hPElzn-2Hqizx?key=3tTunpdgT2tQYTmIdWuK7Q]

LISTEN HERE [https://www.opb.org/article/2024/08/09/think-out-loud-tina-kotek-governor-governor-interview/]

Governor and First Lady visit with the Klamath Tribes and celebrate their new housing for tribal elders.

Governor Kotek at a ribbon cutting ceremony [https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeZjfUt1HCE3jCG0ShsxPHcMVFYh7fw-9SFsUG69y9tfWvUBzPrUb0EmD7O210iq9qnr_KX2Nz5wSH_5nZ4r7L5CjJlPZfS_otSN_YLpHBh8rFFigeg8nLgBeuJOVslLn0DdzZdUY2P0ZDhsYXvmuPefw0v?key=3tTunpdgT2tQYTmIdWuK7Q]

This project in Chiloquin is the latest Project Turnkey site (conversion of an old motel for housing) and another example of the progress Oregon is making on the housing crisis.

Tina attends the Democratic National Convention in Chicago.

Governor Kotek with her fellow women Governors and Julia Louis-Dreyfus [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92654/images/Kotek_Convention.jpg]

Oregon receives more funding to fight climate change!

https://www.opb.org/article/2024/07/22/oregon-awarded-nearly-200-million-dollars-federal-funding-boost-climate-action-programs/ [https://www.opb.org/article/2024/07/22/oregon-awarded-nearly-200-million-dollars-federal-funding-boost-climate-action-programs/] https://www.opb.org/article/2024/07/22/oregon-awarded-nearly-200-million-dollars-federal-funding-boost-climate-action-programs/ [https://www.opb.org/article/2024/07/22/oregon-awarded-nearly-200-million-dollars-federal-funding-boost-climate-action-programs/]

READ THE FULL ARTICLE HERE [https://www.opb.org/article/2024/07/22/oregon-awarded-nearly-200-million-dollars-federal-funding-boost-climate-action-programs/]

Thanks, team. Talk soon!

— Team Tina

name: Family of Bill Pascrell
subject: From the family of Bill Pascrell:
body:
On behalf of our family, thank you so much for your deep support.
Friend,
On behalf of our family, we wanted to reach out to Bill's supporters to thank you personally for your unrelenting support of Bill throughout the years. He went to work each day to fight for you. You can read below about the many priorities Bill fought for and accomplishments Bill achieved thanks to our work together. Bill's obituary also includes information about his funeral service this week:
* * *
Bill Pascrell, Jr. was a husband, a father, a grandfather, a proud American, plain spoken New Jerseyan, a teacher, a veteran, a patriot, a local, state, and federal leader, and most of all a lifelong Patersonian. Each part of his life guided him for over a generation in the United States Congress.
Bill was friends with Presidents. He ate with Prime Ministers. He drank with Premiers. But he was happiest talking with neighbors in North Jersey. He delighted in holding court beside working men and working women. Bill loved his job every day because he loved helping people. He successfully represented one of the most diverse districts in all America because regular Americans of all ethnicities knew he was one of them.
Bill attended St. George’s Elementary School in Paterson and graduated from St. John the Baptist High School. He received an undergraduate degree in journalism and a master’s degree in philosophy, both from his beloved Fordham University. After college he became a teacher and taught in Paramus High School for 12 years. He later served as the President of the Passaic County Community College Board of Trustees.
Bill served his country in the U.S. Army and the U.S. Army Reserve. He received an honorable discharge in 1967.
Bill was a late bloomer to government service. Despite an unbeaten electoral record for decades, he did not start with victory. He tasted early defeat and worked hard to break through. He loved to tell stories about the rough-and-tumble days of Paterson ward politics and the personalities that were involved in Passaic politics in the sixties and seventies. Once rejected by the party bosses, Bill rose to become Passaic County Democratic Chairman, helping rebuild and reinvigorate the organization to great successes.
Bill first became an elected official in 1987 when he was elected to the New Jersey General Assembly, eventually rising to the position of Minority Leader Pro-Tempore. While in Trenton, in 1990 he was elected to his dream job: Mayor. He loved being Mayor of Paterson (with one T, he would remind people on a regular basis). He adored the city’s tapestry of streets and shops and residents and he toiled nonstop to help make all of them better.
Bill was elected to Congress in 1996. In office, he immediately brought a hands-on, local government approach to Washington. His colleagues called him “Mayor” and he was proud of that moniker. Sometimes they called him “Silky” after his hometown. His office gained and then held a reputation as a place where any person could come for assistance on any issue – missing Social Security, fraught immigration status, a pothole – and where none was ever deemed too small. Bill’s favorite events to attend may have been naturalization ceremonies. He smiled ear-to-ear whenever helping swear-in new Americans to our great country.
For nearly two decades, Bill was New Jersey’s only member of the powerful House Ways and Means Committee. On the committee, he was the foremost champion for tax fairness in America. He pushed for a working IRS that would stand up to rich tax cheats. Since 2017, Bill led his allies in New Jersey and New York demanding the end of the state and local tax deduction cap that has crushed our middle class neighbors. On the panel, especially as the Chairman of the Oversight Subcommittee, he held corrupt actors accountable and always stood up for the little guy and gal. Bill routinely reduced cabinet secretaries and agency commissioners to stammering heaps under his intense questions. In his final Congresses, Bill was the lead sponsor of bills to close some of the worst loopholes in the federal tax code.
Bill was an original member of the House Homeland Security Committee. After the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on our nation, Bill became a loud champion for the families who lost loved ones on that terrible day. For over 15 years, he sounded the alarm on growing domestic extremism and begged his colleagues to take notice. Bill was the leading voice in Congress in support of the Nonprofit Security Grant program. Through his hard work, Congress has allocated hundreds of millions of dollars to protect countless churches, synagogues, mosques, temples, and other houses of worship under threat. That work continued through Bill’s last day in office.
Bill was a member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in his early years in office. No one state relies on its roads, rails and bridges more than the densely populated Garden State. Bill delivered, including for an improved interchange at 23/80/46, better bridges along Route 46, as well as new bus depots, revamped rail stations and community jitney buses. Safety was always Bill’s focus. After the tragic crash of Flight 3407 out of Newark, Bill worked closely with his colleagues to finally impose commonsense safety requirements to prevent the pilot fatigue that likely led to the accident. Since the enactment of the law, there has not been a single commercial airline crash in America in 15 years.
As mayor and as congressman Bill loved the police, the firefighters, and first responders. They were often his highest priority. Incredibly, Bill was the leader of both the Law Enforcement Caucus and the Fire Services Caucus in the U.S. House. Not many members of Congress have ever claimed both titles simultaneously.
For too long, firefighters often held bake sales to buy gear and pay for resources. This offended Bill and he did something about it. Bill wrote the Firefighter Investment and Response Enhancement (FIRE) Act which established the first federal program that delivers grant dollars directly to fire departments. Because of Bill’s work, America’s fire departments in communities across the nation have obtained billions to purchase equipment, training, and vehicles needed to serve their communities and save lives. Bill also crafted the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response, or SAFER, grant program that was signed into law in 2003 and which provides additional federal support for local fire departments. He also helped secure federal funds for a new firehouse in the City of Paterson that now bears his name.
Bill led efforts in Congress to protect numerous law enforcement funding. When every Trump budget tried to defund COPS grants, Bill led opposition to save them. His bills signed into law provided bulletproof vests for police, cut red tape, and protected benefits for first responders who give their lives in service to others.
When police and fire leaders in Washington and across our country needed help, they knew Bill’s door was always open to them.
Today, Paterson’s Great Falls are a national park because of Bill. For years he fought in Washington to win the designation. The day it was voted on in Congress, he prowled the floor and worked closely with friends on both sides of the aisle to secure the votes. When it passed, it was one of the proudest moments of his life.
Bill has always fought to protect our environment and combat climate change. He authored laws to support renewable energy, delivered funds to provide clean and safe drinking water, and facilitated the clean-up of contaminated sites through northern New Jersey.
Another proud moment came in the spring of 2012. Facing a brutal primary fight that most so-called experts predicted he would lose, Bill built one of the most impressive coalitions our state has ever seen. He won a landslide. After winning on a Tuesday night, somehow, Bill was back in Washington on Wednesday morning to manage a bill on the House floor. When Bill walked in, he was given a standing ovation from his colleagues. That recognition was one of the sweetest moments of his career.
Bill wore his Italian heritage on his sleeve and his pride informed his leadership. He served for years as the leader of the large Italian American delegation in the Congress. He used his post to strengthen the bond between the U.S. and Italian Republic, and raised his voice to ensure no one ever forgot the role of Italians in America’s past and its future.
Bill was proud to invoke his experience as a public school teacher wherever he went. Up to 2024, his office would regularly hear from Bill’s former students now living in New Jersey and far-flung places. Their memories of his classroom were always warm and fondly recalled.
Even though Bill was one of Congress’s oldest members, his voice was one of its loudest. He acknowledged change and he embraced evolution. By the end of his career, Bill used social media better than most of his colleagues. His clear, passionate messaging was routinely used by the White House and congressional leadership.
Bill’s office was widely seen as one of the most responsive and most innovative for good reason. In Congress as in most places a staff is a reflection of its head. A poor boss will hire those in their image, a good boss will do the same. Bill demanded results and he hired scores of excellent staff members who delivered those results for the people of New Jersey and America. The Pittsburgh Steelers hold the Super Bowl victory record and epitomize excellence. Since 1969 they have had but three head coaches. In his near-three decades in Congress, Bill had three chiefs of staff.
Bill loved baseball. He loved coaching the Democrats’ Congressional Baseball Team. Sometimes his colleagues loved his wisdom, too. He watched the Yankees religiously. He enjoyed a rich cigar and often stayed out late. He savored great movies. He delighted in a nice meal and full conversation. He recently told a group of students his favorite Italian dish was a perfectly cooked artichoke.
With all of his accomplishments what he loved the most was his family. Bill was the beloved husband of Elsie (nee: Botto) Pascrell. Loving father of William J. Pascrell, III(BP3) and his partner Benemina Sancivieri of Roseland, David J. Pascrell and his wife Laura of Montclair and Glenn Pascrell and his wife Magdalena Buczek of Montclair. clean_body: On behalf of our family, thank you so much for your deep support. Friend, On behalf of our family, we wanted to reach out to Bill's supporters to thank you personally for your unrelenting support of Bill throughout the years. He went to work each day to fight for you. You can read below about the many priorities Bill fought for and accomplishments Bill achieved thanks to our work together. Bill's obituary also includes information about his funeral service this week: Bill Pascrell, Jr. was a husband, a father, a grandfather, a proud American, plain spoken New Jerseyan, a teacher, a veteran, a patriot, a local, state, and federal leader, and most of all a lifelong Patersonian. Each part of his life guided him for over a generation in the United States Congress. Bill was friends with Presidents. He ate with Prime Ministers. He drank with Premiers. But he was happiest talking with neighbors in North Jersey. He delighted in holding court beside working men and working women. Bill loved his job every day because he loved helping people. He successfully represented one of the most diverse districts in all America because regular Americans of all ethnicities knew he was one of them. Bill attended St. George’s Elementary School in Paterson and graduated from St. John the Baptist High School. He received an undergraduate degree in journalism and a master’s degree in philosophy, both from his beloved Fordham University. After college he became a teacher and taught in Paramus High School for 12 years. He later served as the President of the Passaic County Community College Board of Trustees. Bill served his country in the U.S. Army and the U.S. Army Reserve. He received an honorable discharge in 1967. Bill was a late bloomer to government service. Despite an unbeaten electoral record for decades, he did not start with victory. He tasted early defeat and worked hard to break through. He loved to tell stories about the rough-and-tumble days of Paterson ward politics and the personalities that were involved in Passaic politics in the sixties and seventies. Once rejected by the party bosses, Bill rose to become Passaic County Democratic Chairman, helping rebuild and reinvigorate the organization to great successes. Bill first became an elected official in 1987 when he was elected to the New Jersey General Assembly, eventually rising to the position of Minority Leader Pro-Tempore. While in Trenton, in 1990 he was elected to his dream job: Mayor. He loved being Mayor of Paterson (with one T, he would remind people on a regular basis). He adored the city’s tapestry of streets and shops and residents and he toiled nonstop to help make all of them better. Bill was elected to Congress in 1996. In office, he immediately brought a hands-on, local government approach to Washington. His colleagues called him “Mayor” and he was proud of that moniker. Sometimes they called him “Silky” after his hometown. His office gained and then held a reputation as a place where any person could come for assistance on any issue – missing Social Security, fraught immigration status, a pothole – and where none was ever deemed too small. Bill’s favorite events to attend may have been naturalization ceremonies. He smiled ear-to-ear whenever helping swear-in new Americans to our great country. For nearly two decades, Bill was New Jersey’s only member of the powerful House Ways and Means Committee. On the committee, he was the foremost champion for tax fairness in America. He pushed for a working IRS that would stand up to rich tax cheats. Since 2017, Bill led his allies in New Jersey and New York demanding the end of the state and local tax deduction cap that has crushed our middle class neighbors. On the panel, especially as the Chairman of the Oversight Subcommittee, he held corrupt actors accountable and always stood up for the little guy and gal. Bill routinely reduced cabinet secretaries and agency commissioners to stammering heaps under his intense questions. In his final Congresses, Bill was the lead sponsor of bills to close some of the worst loopholes in the federal tax code. Bill was an original member of the House Homeland Security Committee. After the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on our nation, Bill became a loud champion for the families who lost loved ones on that terrible day. For over 15 years, he sounded the alarm on growing domestic extremism and begged his colleagues to take notice. Bill was the leading voice in Congress in support of the Nonprofit Security Grant program. Through his hard work, Congress has allocated hundreds of millions of dollars to protect countless churches, synagogues, mosques, temples, and other houses of worship under threat. That work continued through Bill’s last day in office. Bill was a member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in his early years in office. No one state relies on its roads, rails and bridges more than the densely populated Garden State. Bill delivered, including for an improved interchange at 23/80/46, better bridges along Route 46, as well as new bus depots, revamped rail stations and community jitney buses. Safety was always Bill’s focus. After the tragic crash of Flight 3407 out of Newark, Bill worked closely with his colleagues to finally impose commonsense safety requirements to prevent the pilot fatigue that likely led to the accident. Since the enactment of the law, there has not been a single commercial airline crash in America in 15 years. As mayor and as congressman Bill loved the police, the firefighters, and first responders. They were often his highest priority. Incredibly, Bill was the leader of both the Law Enforcement Caucus and the Fire Services Caucus in the U.S. House. Not many members of Congress have ever claimed both titles simultaneously. For too long, firefighters often held bake sales to buy gear and pay for resources. This offended Bill and he did something about it. Bill wrote the Firefighter Investment and Response Enhancement (FIRE) Act which established the first federal program that delivers grant dollars directly to fire departments. Because of Bill’s work, America’s fire departments in communities across the nation have obtained billions to purchase equipment, training, and vehicles needed to serve their communities and save lives. Bill also crafted the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response, or SAFER, grant program that was signed into law in 2003 and which provides additional federal support for local fire departments. He also helped secure federal funds for a new firehouse in the City of Paterson that now bears his name. Bill led efforts in Congress to protect numerous law enforcement funding. When every Trump budget tried to defund COPS grants, Bill led opposition to save them. His bills signed into law provided bulletproof vests for police, cut red tape, and protected benefits for first responders who give their lives in service to others. When police and fire leaders in Washington and across our country needed help, they knew Bill’s door was always open to them. Today, Paterson’s Great Falls are a national park because of Bill. For years he fought in Washington to win the designation. The day it was voted on in Congress, he prowled the floor and worked closely with friends on both sides of the aisle to secure the votes. When it passed, it was one of the proudest moments of his life. Bill has always fought to protect our environment and combat climate change. He authored laws to support renewable energy, delivered funds to provide clean and safe drinking water, and facilitated the clean-up of contaminated sites through northern New Jersey. Another proud moment came in the spring of 2012. Facing a brutal primary fight that most so-called experts predicted he would lose, Bill built one of the most impressive coalitions our state has ever seen. He won a landslide. After winning on a Tuesday night, somehow, Bill was back in Washington on Wednesday morning to manage a bill on the House floor. When Bill walked in, he was given a standing ovation from his colleagues. That recognition was one of the sweetest moments of his career. Bill wore his Italian heritage on his sleeve and his pride informed his leadership. He served for years as the leader of the large Italian American delegation in the Congress. He used his post to strengthen the bond between the U.S. and Italian Republic, and raised his voice to ensure no one ever forgot the role of Italians in America’s past and its future. Bill was proud to invoke his experience as a public school teacher wherever he went. Up to 2024, his office would regularly hear from Bill’s former students now living in New Jersey and far-flung places. Their memories of his classroom were always warm and fondly recalled. Even though Bill was one of Congress’s oldest members, his voice was one of its loudest. He acknowledged change and he embraced evolution. By the end of his career, Bill used social media better than most of his colleagues. His clear, passionate messaging was routinely used by the White House and congressional leadership. Bill’s office was widely seen as one of the most responsive and most innovative for good reason. In Congress as in most places a staff is a reflection of its head. A poor boss will hire those in their image, a good boss will do the same. Bill demanded results and he hired scores of excellent staff members who delivered those results for the people of New Jersey and America. The Pittsburgh Steelers hold the Super Bowl victory record and epitomize excellence. Since 1969 they have had but three head coaches. In his near-three decades in Congress, Bill had three chiefs of staff. Bill loved baseball. He loved coaching the Democrats’ Congressional Baseball Team. Sometimes his colleagues loved his wisdom, too. He watched the Yankees religiously. He enjoyed a rich cigar and often stayed out late. He savored great movies. He delighted in a nice meal and full conversation. He recently told a group of students his favorite Italian dish was a perfectly cooked artichoke. With all of his accomplishments what he loved the most was his family. Bill was the beloved husband of Elsie (nee: Botto) Pascrell. Loving father of William J. There were countless thoughtful and energizing speeches and events throughout the DNC, but First Lady Michelle Obama's call to "do something" has stuck with me the most. Delegates from every state have voted to nominate Vice President Kamala Harris for President and affirm her choice of Governor Tim Walz for Vice President: and now, it is our job to do something. It is an honor to represent our district. Our shared values — working hard, caring for each other, and serving the community — guide my work in Congress to serve the people of Northwest Washington. subject: I’m stressed
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kaine for Virginia
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-tester [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-tester]
Folks—I’m stressed. My campaign team just called me to share that we're still $51,947 short of our August fundraising goal.
I’ll explain more in a moment, but first, I have to ask: Will you make a split donation of any amount right now to help us close the gap before our end-of-month deadline? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-tester]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-tester]
Mitch McConnell is flooding in millions of dollars to smear my record and boost his handpicked candidate. Unfortunately, these attacks are working: The latest polls have this race wide open.
Look, I’ve never been your typical politician. I’m a farmer. I grew up in a twenty-four-by-thirty-six foot house. I still farm the land my parents homesteaded 100 years ago. (Sharla and I are harvesting as we speak.)
I try every day to do right by the people of Montana. That means standing up to anybody—including Mitch McConnell and his special interests—to improve health care for veterans, lower prescription drug costs, and protect Medicare and Social Security.
But if I don’t get more grassroots support before the end of August, there’s a very real chance our team could miss our goal. Mitch McConnell and outside groups are spending nearly $90 million to buy this Senate seat—and the only thing that can stop them is you.
As much as I hate asking, I have to: Can I count on you to make a split donation of $10 before our end-of-month goal? When we win in November, it’ll be because of folks like you. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-tester]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tk-2024-tester]
Thanks for your support.
—Jon Tester

body:
[https://als-totem.s3.amazonaws.com/core/spacer.gif] Hi! [https://als-totem.s3.amazonaws.com/core/spacer.gif]
I just arrived home in Albany after an incredible week in Chicago—I left the DNC feeling so energized, so inspired, and so hopeful about what’s to come.
But I want to echo what Governor Walz said on Wednesday night: We cannot be complacent. We’ve got to roll up our sleeves, get to work, and leave it all on the field.
We have 73 days until Election Day. 73 days to do everything we can to elect my friend, Vice President Kamala Harris and save our razor-thin Senate majority. Can you make a donation today—right now—to elect Kamala Harris and help keep the Senate blue? [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/kg_kh?refcode=2024_08_24_ND]
These past four years have shown our country what it looks like when Democrats govern. We made transformative investments in American manufacturing through the CHIPS Act. We passed the first meaningful gun safety legislation in decades —including my legislation to make gun trafficking a federal crime, getting illegal weapons off our streets. We cut the cost of prescription drugs, and took meaningful action to address climate change.
And I know that with Kamala Harris in the White House and Democratic majorities in Congress, the sky is truly the limit. We can restore reproductive rights nationwide, and finally enshrine the Equal Rights Amendment in the Constitution. We can keep our communities safe, lower health care costs, and ensure that no family working full-time is struggling to make ends meet.
So please: If you’re feeling as inspired as me, make a donation to elect Kamala Harris and power my work to save our Senate majority. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/kg_kh?refcode=2024_08_24_ND]

Thank you for stepping up, and for not taking anything for granted.
With hope and gratitude,
Kirsten

Our voter registration campaign made a huge difference in 2022 and 2023. We've got no choice but to keep it going for 2024 and stop any chance of losing more of our voting rights to cynical conspiracy theorists spreading lies.

This is probably the hardest email I’ve ever written.

| |

| | | | | | | Friend --
I wish things would have gone a different way...
| **_Democrat Vicente Gonzalez holds back Republican surge, returns 34th Congressional District to Democratic control._**
---

This is probably the hardest email I've ever written.

**I 'm Mayra Flores, the America First Hispanic woman running in the biggest race in the nation.**

After we made history and flipped a blue seat red for the first time in 100 years, the Democrats threw the kitchen sink at me, **and I had to concede my race. **

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=df0fcfa3d4844663a1d0889b639e4189&_e=7CH8wbK090KNL4c_4PxQBjVmCFOQxXTYvO1dumisRYozfthDZcSHfOqqut2lACtObmwOKuZbYNaLw9TdkZnqt_sxLhfN-iqxVgUGsVi_w6yptrTvsBgJTk9tM5eN3lqdGB0fXeiuiS4wNvI5qiNHEYZ9bpHHYix42u-AQ5nZQu3kfVSCFWIX-BTwZNOLdgsT96l30wgu7nFvZP-LtWRrSGsQf7u7y8awJxz8epnII48NmxIOJ3n77uN18SwL1AemlvzCcVct99fE0F8tLopTMtFzghRpF-IYCYqObYFcnotUTJpCeCpd-Ot1bH8LIr1hzhIme1uv3ARhAv-2aq5zAZZU57dqdLEyawL3MWD8SvEL3vJf_YyDT7VTcb2FMLbRcvAfknPnM4QcQb-1YQO1zc2022stHBR6F_eTwuQXwCY%3D)

---
Everyone expected me to just walk away - _but I 'm not someone who ever, ever gives up._

I'm taking a leap of faith here and have thrown my name on the ballot once again.

The Democrats overpowered us in this race before - _and now all indicators are pointing toward this election being a complete toss-up._

My stomach is in knots - **the Democrats have already raised an astonishing $30 MILLION, and Kamala just raised $80 million bucks**(I know, I can't believe anyone would give her money either...but they do).

**That 's why I'm humbly asking for your help: _[Will you step up and chip in just a few bucks in the next hour to help us counter this massive Left-wing onslaught?](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=df0fcfa3d4844663a1d0889b639e4189&_e=7CH8wbK090KNL4c_4PxQBjVmCFOQxXTYvO1dumisRYozfthDZcSHfOqqut2lACtObmwOKuZbYNaLw9TdkZnqt_sxLhfN-iqxVgUGsVi_w6yptrTvsBgJTk9tM5eN3lqdGB0fXeiuiS4wNvI5qiNHEYZ9bpHHYix42u-AQ5nZQu3kfVSCFWIX-BTwZNOLdgsT96l30wgu7nFvZP-LtWRrSGsQf7u7y8awJxz8epnII48NmxIOJ3n77uN18SwL1AemlvzCcVct99fE0F8tLopTMkQ0p5EhK0yigt54C_k8Gf6TtKGyJQKjyX4cb0LGhOHigWBlNHaYkkU7CVTj6HTRBr9vfR1vUxwhOheD56TJBBds9_pXNCqNucmmiMBVUsPEApQzKgNmGgwdGFY-kmKDaEbjq_EUHMGPknlU3migZXM%3D "Will you step up and chip in just a few bucks in the next hour to help us counter this massive Left-wing onslaught?")_**

I'll just tell you: I'm afraid to see what happens if this email doesn't work.

**The Democrats & the media hacks are terrified of me - that's because as a young Hispanic female, I obliterate every woke narrative they push. So, they will truly do anything to destroy me.**

The Democrats know that if they lose the Hispanic vote, it's over for them. _Forever._

We're going to keep Arizona blue
Peter, since our primary victory my team and I have been hustling to expand and build on our voter mobilization and registration efforts here in Phoenix. The path to keeping the White House and retaining our Senate majority runs right through here, and we're going to fight for it every day.
Among the congratulatory messages my team and I have received since Tuesday have been folks letting us know to take time to relax, enjoy the win, and take our foot off the gas. But that's simply not possible. There is a target on our community, with MAGA and right-wing extremists already hard at work with voter suppression tactics here and across the state.
If we take even a second to let up, they will pounce. I refuse to give them an inch in the battle to keep AZ blue and elect Kamala Harris. That's why I'm reaching out to you today, Peter.
We set a goal of raising $20,000 online in the first week after our primary victory and now we are only $5,814 short. Can you rush a contribution today to help us reach our goal? It’s her legacy I’m carrying forward when I walk onto the House floor, Peter. Because working people know – we’re in this together. But let’s be real: You shouldn’t have to be working class to care about working class priorities. You don’t need to be rejected by an apartment, or become houseless, or drive Uber to make ends meet – all of which I’ve done – to know that our economy isn’t working for everybody. Derek,

While most of you likely know me from my time in Congress working to hold
Donald Trump accountable for his attacks on democracy, something you may
not know is that I like to do stand-up comedy.

I’m not saying I’m good at it, mind you, but I love going on Bill Maher,
or Stephen Colbert’s show, or Seth Myers, or any of the late-night comedy
shows. And I do stand-up events at the Improv in Hollywood. These days, if
we can’t laugh a little, I think we would all go mad.

Don’t worry, I won’t be quitting my day job anytime soon. But I do like to
laugh and make others laugh too. And I’m a big fan of the Big Lebowski.
When I was last in the Oval Office with President Biden, I looked at the
beautiful blue oval rug and told him: “Mr. President, this rug really ties
the whole room together.”

I also think comedy and comedy shows are a good way to bring new people
into the political process. Some of the most important and biting
observations about our modern political life are made through comedy, and
it pulls in a lot of young people in the audience.

And humor can be a very powerful political weapon, used to disarm a
political attack or point out an obvious irony or hypocrisy. Like when JD
Vance complained about being called schoolyard names, I said that “shifty
Schiff, pencil neck, and watermelon head” would like a word with him.

It would mean a lot to have your support in this race, because every donation goes a long way. Even $12.
So, will you split $12 or more between my campaign and Seth Moulton to help us reach our goal so I can bring this race home? We’ve got less than 100 days until the election, so let’s get it done. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/moulton-tester]

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/91456801/493908189/-2125777536?amount=3&refcode=UTS_FR_90DO_240824_2_1_Schiff&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5NDc2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjA3MzI0MmM3LTRlNjItZWYxMS05OTFhLTYwNDViZGRiZmM0YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=J34IJfUY75XztGaNdyL10tVe7_V_fHB3bp2Rj54-jZA=)
That's me in 1985 — just 24 years old at my law school graduation, fresh off a student research assistant job for Professor Laurence Tribe, thinking that I had just completed the toughest challenge of my academic career. Well, up to that point, anyway. (The bar exam was still a few weeks away).
Some years later, I would become an Assistant United States Attorney, and successfully prosecute the first FBI agent charged with espionage, Richard Miller, for spying for the Soviet Union.
As a new graduate of law school, I could never have imagined I would handle a case like that.
Or that I would later investigate a president who also betrayed our country ...
...lead his impeachment and Senate trial...
...serve on the January 6 Committee...
...get kicked off the Intelligence Committee by a craven Speaker of the House for doing the above...
...and get censured by extreme partisan MAGA House Republicans under the personal threat of that corrupt president...
Life leads us in uncertain and fortuitous ways. I’m fortunate that at a time when our country has been in trouble, and our democracy at risk, I have been in a position to help do something about it.
In the Senate, I hope to do even more.

The campaign to take back America is underway. We are fighting for the America First agenda and to elect true conservatives loyal to President Trump. | **Joe Biden and Kamala Harris are the worst political duo in modern American history, Fellow Patriot.**
